findings.passage: “The right to vote is a powerful underpinning of American democracy, and this legislation protects that right while offering eligible citizens multiple and straightforward opportunities to legally cast their ballot,” Burgum said in a statement. “House Bill 1369 strengthens the integrity of our elections by ensuring all voters have proper identification while allowing those without current or complete forms of ID to provide supplemental documents to verify their eligibility.”
findings.note: Statement issued by the governor when signing North Dakota HB 1369; quoted in a University of Minnesota Election Academy post that reprints a news report. Says the bill requires proper ID while letting voters with outdated or incomplete ID add other documents.
subjects: supplemental documents for voters with incomplete ID

findings.note: As North Dakota governor he signed HB 1369, which amends the state's voter ID law. News coverage says it was signed despite a federal lawsuit and a judge's earlier ruling. Per the same post, a voter with outdated or incomplete ID can add a document such as a utility bill. Official legislature page could not be reached.
subjects: supplemental documents for voters with incomplete ID
